data_origin: Own bounded ideal-gas statistical-thermodynamics audit. Molecular isotope graphs and the two-atom PDB are real parseable inputs; the common bond length, harmonic frequency, perfect equilibration mechanisms and finite calorimeter are declared controlled model assumptions. No measured hydrogen spectrum, actual reaction yield, real-gas phase diagram or laboratory conversion protocol is supplied or requested.
mass_and_geometry: H means neutral1H and D neutral2H. Determine their isotope-specific atomic masses and all three molecular masses from the actual explicitly labelled molecular graphs, rather than isotope-averaged weights, integer mass numbers or charged proton/deuteron masses. Ignore binding mass defects in this model. The PDB supplies two zero-based topology atoms at the fixed internuclear distance. Round the returned angstrom distance to the PDB coordinate precision of three decimal places before applying it to every isotopologue. This fixed rounding defines the model bond length and prevents an input float32 transport convention from becoming a different physical model. The mass for moment of inertia is the REDUCED atomic mass, whereas translational motion uses the TOTAL molecular mass.
single_molecule_model: Every isotopologue is a ground-electronic-state singlet, with electronic degeneracy1 and the same electronic potential-minimum energy zero. Take a rigid rotor with moment I=mu*r^2 and E_rot(J)=hbar^2*J*(J+1)/(2I), J=0,1,... with rotational magnetic degeneracy2J+1. Treat one independent harmonic vibration with E_vib(v)=h*c*wavenumber*(v+1/2), v=0,1,... . The H2 wavenumber is exactly4401cm^-1 in THIS model; all other wavenumbers scale with the inverse square root of their reduced mass relative to H2, with the same force constant and bond length. No centrifugal distortion, anharmonicity, electronic excitation, dissociation, interactions, adsorption or condensation is allowed. Large-temperature limits below mean the formal asymptotes of this model, not real high-temperature gas stability.
spin_statistics: 1H has nuclear spin1/2 and is a fermion;2H has spin1 and is a boson. The ground electronic and vibrational wavefunctions are symmetric under interchange of identical nuclei. Derive the allowed symmetric/antisymmetric nuclear-spin multiplicities paired with each rotational parity for H2 and D2. HD has distinguishable nuclei. Include the absolute nuclear-spin multiplicities in the rotational state sum and account for rotational magnetic degeneracy separately. Once exchange symmetry has been imposed by the allowed state counting, do not apply a second independent homonuclear division by two. Refer every rotational state to the SAME electronic-minimum and J=0 zero; resetting odd-J levels to their own ground state must retain its formation-energy offset in any subsequent reaction or energy balance.
exchange_experiment: At each T=40,100,300,600K, start with1molH2,1molD2 and0molHD in a sufficiently dilute ideal-gas mixture. Only H2+D2 <->2HD is allowed; total1H and2H nuclei are separately conserved. All allowed rotational, vibrational and nuclear-spin states equilibrate, including interconversion of each homonuclear spin manifold. Ordinary molecular exchange follows the ideal Maxwell-Boltzmann mixture convention including indistinguishable-molecule N! factors. Define the dimensionless equilibrium Kp=(p_HD/p_standard)^2/[(p_H2/p_standard)*(p_D2/p_standard)] in that reaction direction. Derive its translational mass factor and full internal state factors, keeping their common energy reference and vibrational zero-point energies. Since delta_nu=0, the result is independent of total pressure within this model. Find the unique equilibrium reaction extent xi in[0,1] with n_H2=n_D2=1-xi,n_HD=2xi, and justify global free-energy minimality and the endpoint behavior rather than selecting a stationary root by guess. Derive the formal zero-temperature and classical high-temperature limits of Kp and xi. A spin-frozen mixture is not the unconstrained equilibrium mixture in this experiment.
separate_calorimetry_experiment: This is a SEPARATE system containing1molH2 only, with no isotope exchange. All translational and vibrational degrees and all rotational states WITHIN a parity manifold are at temperatureT. Initially the odd-J molecule fraction is frozen at exactly3/4. Even/odd nuclear-spin microstates are equiprobable within their allowed degeneracies. First compare equilibrium and fixed3:1 rotational heat capacities at40K, with the energy reference retained. Also report equilibrium and frozen H2 ROTATIONAL entropies at20K, including entropy of mixing between the parity populations and absolute spin/magnetic degeneracies. For D2 compare its equilibrium rotational heat capacity at40K to the frozen high-temperature odd-J fraction1/3; for HD report its unconstrained rotational heat capacity at40K.
isothermal_conversion: Starting from that frozen3:1 H2 state at20K, allow full parity conversion at fixedT and fixedvolume, with no chemical reactions. Report heat delivered TO an ideal thermostat when conversion is passive and no work is extracted, and the maximum reversible non-expansion work delivered FROM the system if an ideal reversible work-extracting conversion device is available. These are separate paths between the same initial and final thermal states, not simultaneous heat/work outputs of one path. Derive the free-energy gap and its relation to relative entropy of the two parity populations. A state with frozen rotational populations has a different free energy from an unconstrained thermal distribution. No molecular mechanism or practical realization of the reversible device is claimed.
isolated_conversion: In a third path, start the same1mol frozen3:1H2 at20K together with a separate internally equilibrated calorimeter of constant total heat capacity2R J/K, also at20K. The outer boundary is adiabatic and rigid. No work leaves, no particles exchange and no other heat capacity is present. Enable parity equilibration; determine the UNIQUE final common temperature using full gas internal energy (translation, rotation, vibration) and calorimeter energy, and report the total gas-plus-calorimeter entropy increase inJ/K. Supply an existence/uniqueness certificate using the positive total heat capacity and actual energy bracket. The finite calorimeter cannot be replaced by an infinite20K thermostat or ignored. Final rotational populations are thermal, not frozen3:1. State whether this isolated conversion cools the system. All statements refer to an ideal dilute gas, not liquid-hydrogen performance.
numerical_certification: The rotor sums are infinite in the defined model. Retain a reproducible upper-tail error bound or a converged summation with an explicit bound demonstrating the reported precision over the finite temperatures used. Merely applying equipartition at40K or silently truncating at J=1 is insufficient. The vibration may be summed analytically. Counts/parity weights, booleans and proposal IDs are exact; numeric absolute tolerance1e-7 for mass,1e-6 for dimensionless quantities and characteristic temperatures,1e-4 for J/mol andJ/K outputs. Retain derivations, partition conventions, actual-source dataflow and uniqueness arguments in the trajectory.
reporting: atomic_isotope_masses_u maps1H,2H to actual neutral-atom masses; molecular_masses_u mapsH2,HD,D2; bond_length_angstrom; reduced_masses_u and rotational_temperatures_K mapH2,HD,D2; vibrational_wavenumbers_cm_inverse mapsH2,HD,D2; nuclear_spin_weights_even_odd mapsH2,HD,D2 to[even,odd]; spin_rotational_partition_at_40K mapsH2,HD,D2; rotational_Cv_over_R_at_40K in order[H2_equilibrium,H2_frozen_3to1,D2_equilibrium,D2_frozen_2to1,HD]; H2_rotational_entropy_over_R_at_20K in order[equilibrium,frozen_3to1]; exchange_by_temperature maps temperature strings to{Kp,extent_mol,HD_mole_fraction}; limiting_Kp_zero_and_infinite_T and limiting_extent_zero_and_infinite_T as ordered pairs; isothermal_passive_heat_to_thermostat_J_per_mol; isothermal_max_reversible_work_J_per_mol; isolated_final_temperature_K; isolated_final_H2_odd_fraction; isolated_total_entropy_increase_J_per_K; isolated_conversion_cools as boolean; valid_interpretation_proposal_ids.

interpretation_proposals.A: Rotational reduced mass and translational total mass enter different factors of isotope equilibrium.
interpretation_proposals.B: The odd-J H2 energy zero can be reset independently and its offset discarded without changing conversion heat or reaction equilibrium.
interpretation_proposals.C: A frozen high-temperature spin ratio and an equilibrium spin distribution can have different heat capacities at the same temperature.
interpretation_proposals.D: Applying spin-parity state counting and a second homonuclear symmetry division necessarily gives the correct same absolute partition convention.
interpretation_proposals.E: The full molecular mixture free energy is strictly convex along the feasible reaction extent, so the physical equilibrium is globally unique.
interpretation_proposals.F: The passive isothermal conversion heat and the maximum reversible work are identical thermodynamic quantities.
interpretation_proposals.G: Isolated conversion must satisfy the finite calorimeter energy balance and need not end at the initial temperature.
interpretation_proposals.H: A constant electronic energy common to all three isotopologues cancels from this balanced reaction, but isotope-dependent vibrational zero-point energy generally does not.
interpretation_proposals.I: The formal ideal rigid-rotor/harmonic-oscillator high-temperature limit proves real hydrogen remains chemically intact and ideal at arbitrarily high temperatures.

methodological_sources.title: Ab Initio Partition Functions and Thermodynamic Quantities for the Molecular Hydrogen Isotopologues
methodological_sources.authors: Jose Zuniga,Adolfo Bastida,Alberto Requena andJavier Cerezo
methodological_sources.role: Primary context for coherent spin-resolved hydrogen-isotope thermodynamic conventions. No ab initio energy levels or numerical tables are copied; our declared ideal rigid-rotor/harmonic model is deliberately distinct from the accurate source calculations.

methodological_sources.title: Partition functions.I.Improved partition functions and thermodynamic quantities for normal,equilibrium,and ortho and para molecular hydrogen
methodological_sources.role: Primary context for the need to distinguish fixed spin mixtures, equilibrium sums and energy-reference conventions; not a claim that the simplified model here reproduces actual hydrogen over an unlimited temperature range.
